concepts.title: Three Major Landforms
concepts.definition: Land takes three major forms: mountains rising high with steep slopes, plateaus standing as raised flat lands, and plains lying low and level; a road trip from Chhota Nagpur to Almora crosses all three.
concepts.key_idea: The same journey can climb a plateau, cross a plain and wind up a mountain, meeting new life at each step.

concepts.title: Life in the Mountains
concepts.definition: Mountains have thin air, steep slopes and cold climate; people terrace the slopes, rear sheep or grow fruit, and mountain culture, from pilgrim routes to mountain homes, grows out of this hard, beautiful life.
concepts.key_idea: Mountains both challenge and shelter: they test travel and farming yet guard rivers and forests.

concepts.title: Life on Plateaus and Plains
concepts.definition: Plateaus are raised flatlands, often rich in minerals and suited to grazing or special crops, while plains, level and watered by rivers, carry the densest farms, towns and transport routes.
concepts.key_idea: Flat land is easy land: plains feed and house the most people, plateaus store minerals beneath.

concepts.title: The Hymn to the Earth: Landforms in Culture
concepts.definition: The chapter opens with the Atharva Veda's hymn to the Earth, which calls the land our mother bearing heights, slopes and plains; landforms are thus part of prayer and culture, not just geography.
concepts.key_idea: Ancient verses saw the Earth as a mother to be respected, binding geography with gratitude.

worked_examples.question_pattern: Why do mountains remain thinly populated compared with plains?

solution_template.explain: Steep slopes, thin soil and cold make farming and building hard.
Level, watered plains grow food and towns easily, so people gather there instead.

worked_examples.question_pattern: What does the hymn to the earth teach about how we should treat land?

solution_template.explain: The Earth is called a mother bearing heights, slopes and plains for our good.
Treating land as a mother means using its riches with care and thanks, not plunder.
